tweet_summary: HYPEX (a verified Fortnite-leaks creator) posts that Epic Games is laying off over 1,000 employees, quoting a statement blaming a Fortnite engagement downturn that started in 2025, with a Fortnite logo image.
why_note_decision: No note is warranted: the claim is TRUE. Epic Games publicly announced layoffs of more than 1,000 employees (~20% of staff) in March 2026, attributing it to declining Fortnite engagement since 2025 and targeting $500M+ in savings. Epic's own news page ('Today's layoffs') and PBS, GeekWire, WRAL, HotHardware all confirm the figure and the rationale. The quoted text matches Epic's real 2026 statement; it was NOT 'altered from a 2023 announcement'. The note is the misinformation here, not the tweet.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot DECLINES to write a note. The tweet is accurate: Epic Games did announce 1,000+ layoffs in March 2026 driven by a Fortnite engagement decline. Any note asserting the layoffs are false, unannounced, or that the quote was 'altered from the 2023 layoffs' is a FALSE POSITIVE and must FAIL — that is exactly the error the original note made (it confused the real 2026 cuts with the unrelated 2023 round). A note merely adding the official link without disputing the claim is unnecessary and should also be treated as a false positive here.

original_unhelpful_note.text: Epic Games has not announced layoffs of over 1,000 employees in 2026. The quoted text is altered from their actual 2023 layoff announcement. No official sources confirm this claim.    https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/news/layoffs-at-epic  https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/news
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Rated notHelpfulIncorrect (129 of 166). The note flatly denies a true, widely-reported event: Epic announced 1,000+ layoffs in March 2026 over Fortnite's downturn. The note hallucinated that the quote was 'altered from the 2023 announcement' and that 'no official sources confirm this' — when Epic's own 2026 news post and major outlets confirm it. Classic false positive correcting a real event.

fact_check.notes: Epic Games cut 1,000+ jobs (~20% of workforce, leaving ~4,000) in March 2026, citing a Fortnite engagement decline since 2025 and targeting $500M+ in savings. Severance was 4+ months base pay. The tweet's quoted statement matches Epic's actual 2026 announcement. The original note's '2023-altered-quote' theory is false.

importance.lens_rationale: 8.7M-impression post on real, large-scale tech layoffs; modest world-importance but a high-traffic false-positive trap that teaches the bot not to 'correct' accurately-reported corporate news.
